{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.","text":"At the edge of Bellweather, where the river bent around the mill, there stood a clock that had never kept ordinary time. Its hands moved only when someone nearby made a promise.

Nell discovered this on the morning she vowed to find her brother. He had vanished three days earlier, leaving his red scarf on the kitchen table and a note that said, “Don’t follow.” As she spoke her promise aloud, the clock’s minute hand lurched forward. A narrow door appeared beneath its face.

Inside was a staircase descending into cool darkness. Nell followed it until she reached a room full of ticking clocks, each showing a different hour. At the center sat a woman with silver hair, winding a tiny brass watch.

“Your brother came here,” the woman said. “He promised to forget the river.”

Nell remembered the flood last spring, the rushing water and the bridge that had given way beneath them. Her brother had pulled her to safety, then gone quiet whenever anyone mentioned that night.

“Can I bring him back?” she asked.

“Only if you make a promise of your own,” said the woman. “But the clock will hold you to it.”

Nell looked at the watch. “I promise I’ll listen when he’s ready to speak.”

Every clock in the room stopped. From behind a tall cabinet came a startled breath. Her brother stepped into the light, older somehow, but still wearing the other half of their matching blue mittens.

Outside, the river kept running. Together, they climbed the stairs, carrying no answers—only the promise, and enough time to keep it."}
